title: US venture deal value reaches record $515.8B as exits fail to keep pace
source_used: SiliconANGLE (full text read), reporting the PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor released the same day
key_facts: US venture deal value reached $515.8 billion in the first nine months of 2026, about 44% past the previous annual record with a quarter still to go.
AI accounts for a record 82.7% of the year's deal value, though its share fell to 65.9% in the third quarter.
Third-quarter deal value fell about 40% to $98.4 billion; Databricks took the quarter's largest check at $5 billion.
SpaceX's $60 billion all-stock purchase of Anysphere, the Cursor developer, was 53.1% of third-quarter exit value; without it exits come to $53 billion, the lowest since late 2024.
Startups valued at $1 billion or more reached a record 992 at the end of September, with a combined value of $5.7 trillion.
US venture firms raised $108.5 billion across 699 funds so far this year; 211 emerging firms closed a fund, against 927 in 2022.
quote_evidence: Giant artificial intelligence rounds have pushed U.S. venture capital deal value about 44% past its previous annual record with a quarter still to go, according to the quarterly PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor report released today, but the exits needed to return that money to investors have not kept pace.
Strip it out and the quarter’s exits come to $53 billion, which would be the lowest since late 2024.
“This year’s numbers will look like a boom at the top line,” Tarhuni said.
why_it_matters_hint: Founders and investors: most of the market is not getting money back through listings or sales.
notes: SiliconANGLE read in full; the PitchBook-NVCA report itself was not read. Left out of the summary: Anthropic's IPO slipping to November and OpenAI's reported IPO position.
